# **PREFACE**

This is a guide to using the AGILA CATalog app, written for the people who use it every day. You do **not** need to know anything technical to use this manual.

## **Roles**

The app has three kinds of users. Each one can do everything the one before it can, **plus more**:

| Role | What they do | Where to read |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| **Volunteer** | Go out, count cats, log them in census sessions | [Part 1](#part-1---volunteer) |
| **Manager** | All of the above, plus review and approve what volunteers submit, and manage the cat database | [Part 2](#part-2---manager) |
| **Administrator** | All of the above, plus manage people, regions, and the Google Sheets connection | [Part 3](#part-3---admin) |

 

Each Part is **self-contained** — it repeats what the roles before it cover. If you are a volunteer, you only ever need Part 1\. If you are an administrator, Part 3 has everything.

**Developers only:** setup, deployment, and how the Google Sheets sync works under the hood live in this GitHub repo: [https://github.com/legnspice/agila-app](https://github.com/legnspice/agila-app) — start with `docs/development.md`, and see `docs/operations/gsheets-sync-setup.md` for the sync itself. Nothing in this manual requires a developer, a terminal, or code.

## **The Idea Behind The App**

The **app is the primary, authoritative place to manage cats in Ateneo.** The CATalog Google Sheets that AGILA’s Animal Management Department (originally) uses are kept in **two-way sync** with the app:

* **The app updates the sheet.** Anything you add or change in the app appears in the matching Google Sheet automatically, every few minutes.  
* **The sheet can update the app.** Edits made directly in the sheet (by someone with edit access) flow *back* into the app on the next sync. If the same cat was changed in both places, the **most recent edit wins**.

So the sheet is a **live mirror you can also write to**.

**The guidance for everyone is still simple: do your work in the app.**

* The app is the intended, safest way to add and edit cats. It checks your input and keeps everything consistent.  
*  Editing the spreadsheet directly is a **manager fallback** for emergencies (see Part 2\) — not the normal workflow.  
* **Volunteers** are given **view-only** access to the sheet, so for them it's just for looking — all their work happens in the app anyway.

If you remember one thing: **the app is the authority; the sheet stays in step with it both ways, but routine work belongs in the app.**

 

## **Definition of Terms**

| Term | What it means |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Cat / entry** | One cat's record — its photo, details, health, and location. |
| **Census** | A count of the cats in an area at a point in time. |
| **Session** | One trip out to count cats in one location. Has a **Census No.** and a list of cats you logged. |
| **Census No.** | The automatic number given to each session, so they can be referred to in order. |
| **Catalog No.** | The number in the **first column** of a region's sheet, identifying one cat *on that sheet*. Not the same as the Census No. Each region numbers its own cats from 1. |
| **Region / Location** | A named zone on campus (e.g. *GATE 3* , *ARETE* ). Every cat and every session belongs to one. |
| **TNVR** | **T**rap– **N**euter– **V**accinate– **R**eturn — the program for humanely managing the cat population. |
| **Sociability** | How comfortable a cat is around people: *Domesticated* , *Tame* , or *Feral* . |
| **Submitted / Unfinished** | A session you've sent for review is *Submitted* ; one you're still working on is *Unfinished* . |
| **Review / Merge** | When a manager checks a submitted session and combines duplicate sightings of the same cat. |
| **Sync** | The automatic background process that keeps the app and the Google Sheets matching — in **both** directions, every few minutes. |
| **Catalog** | The public-facing list of adoptable cats. Anyone can view it without signing in, and search engines can find it. Each cat has its own shareable page. |
| **Adoptable** | A switch on each cat (Database → General) that decides whether it appears in the public Catalog. |
| **Expired** *(vaccination)* | The cat was vaccinated, but more than a year ago, so a booster is due. Not the same as unvaccinated. |
| **Unknown** | Nobody has recorded an answer yet. The app says "Unknown" rather than guessing — it does **not** mean "no". |
| **Frozen / Retired** | *Frozen* is a temporary safety pause on the sync that you undo with **Unfreeze**. *Retired* is the deliberate, permanent end of the sync (see 3.3). |

 

# **PART 1 \- VOLUNTEER** {#part-1---volunteer}

As a volunteer, your job is the **census**: go to a location, find the cats, and log each one in the app. Everything you need is in the **Sessions** tab.

## **1.1 Getting in**

1\.       Go to [https://ateneanagila.vercel.app/](https://ateneanagila.vercel.app/)  
2\.    Click Log In in the homepage’s navigation bar.  
3\.    Tap **Sign in with Google**.  
4\.       Choose your account.

You must be **invited first** — an administrator adds your email to the app before you can sign in. If you sign in and see a message that you're *not onboarded*, your email hasn't been added yet. Ask an administrator to add you (see Part 3).

![][image2]

**Figure 1:** *Sign-In Screen*

## **1.2 What you can see**

You can then proceed onto the dashboard. As a volunteer you have four tabs:

* **Overview** — an overall statistics dashboard: breaks down population into categories  
* **TNVR** — a specific statistics dashboard: how much of the cat population has been neutered/spayed (the **TNVR Score**), with a breakdown by sex, shown for all locations or one at a time.  
* **Database** — every cat's full record. You can **look but not change** — the detail screens are read-only for volunteers.  
* **Sessions** — your main workspace. This is where you run a census. 

## **1.3 Starting a census session**

1\.       Go to the **Sessions** tab.  
2\.       Tap **Create New**.  
3\.       Choose the **Location** (region) you're counting.  
4\.       The app creates the session and gives it a **Census No.** You can now add cats.

![][image3]

**Figure 2:** *Sessions Tab*

You don't have to finish in one sitting. A session you haven't submitted shows as **Unfinished** in your Sessions list with a **Continue** button — tap it to pick up where you left off.

## **1.4 Adding a cat to the session**

1\.       Inside the session, tap the **\+** button (the orange circle, bottom-right on mobile, or **Add entry** on desktop).  
2\.       The **Add Entry** form opens. Fill in what you can — **every field is optional except a location**, and the location is already set from the session.

![][image4]

**Figure 3:** *Add Entry Form*

**The photo** (top of the form):

* Tap **Take photo** to use your camera, or **Choose file** to pick an existing picture.  
* After picking, you can **drag the photo to reposition it** so the cat is centred.  
* **Rotate** turns the photo a quarter-turn at a time. Use it when a photo comes out sideways or upside-down — common when the phone was held at an angle. Keep tapping to go all the way round.  
* **Retake**, **File**, or **Remove** let you change your mind.

***Note:** repositioning and rotating only change how the photo is **framed** — the original picture is always kept whole underneath. You can re-frame the same photo as many times as you like without any loss in quality, and you can always go back.*

**\[SCREENSHOT NEEDED: the photo editor showing the Rotate control\]**

***Note:** Ideal posture for identification: face, side and tail are clearly visible.*

**The details** (scroll through form):

1. **Name** \- Optional — a nickname if the cat has one.

2. **Color** \- The cat's coat (e.g. Calico, Orange Tabby). Leave as Unknown if unsure.

**![][image5]**  
***Note:** Tabby means there are stripes, Calico has three colors (orange, white, gray/brown) which are easily distinguishable, Tortie has three colors (orange, white, gray/brown) which are not easily distinguishable, Torbie is a tabby that has three colors (orange, white, gray/brown) which are not easily distinguishable*

3. **Size/Age** \- *Neonatal*, *Kitten*, *Juvenile*, or *Adult* .

![][image6]

*Neonates (\~0-3 weeks, \~6 in / hand size) are newborns so they can barely walk and their ears are still folded.* 

*Kittens (\~4-8 weeks, \~ less than 12 in / smaller than a foot) are still small but they can walk and their ears are not folded.*  
*![][image7]*  
*Juveniles (\~4-6 months, \~ a bit more than 1 ft) are bigger than kittens and have more developed eyes (ex: born with blue, color changes to yellow). At this age, sex can be identified since genitals for males are developed already.* 

*Adults (\~1 year, \~ 1.5 ft) are bigger than a juvenile.*  
*![][image8]*

*Sample timeline of a Catenean:*

* *Born at the start of the 1st Semester: Neonatal*  
* *Middle of the 1st Semester: Kitten*  
* *After Christmas Break / Start of the 2nd Semester: Juvenile*  
* *Middle of the 2nd Semester: Juvenile*  
* *After Summer Break / Start of the next 1st Semester: Adult*


4. **Sex** \- Male or Female 

![][image9]

5. **Sociability** \-  If the cats are affectionate and/or approach you, they are Domesticated. If the cats do not care when you step towards them, they are Tame. If they tense up or immediately run away when you step towards them, they are Feral.  
6. **Condition**   
* If they look like the cats below, write “Sick”. Otherwise, write “Healthy”.

| ![][image10] | ![][image11] |
| :---: | :---: |
| *Mange* | *Respiratory infection (mucus, sneezing)* |

| ![][image12] | ![][image13] |
| :---: | :---- |
| *Kidney problems (malnourished, drooling, unkempt fur, increased thirst/dehydration, lack of appetite)* |  |

* If they look like the cats below, write “**Injured**”.


| ![][image14] | ![][image15] |
| :---: | :---- |
| *Scars (left) and Wounds (right) from cat fighting or human-induced harm* |  |

| ![][image16] | ![][image17] |
| ----- | :---- |
| *Eye infection (left) is sick while Eye injury (right) is injured * **Neutered** \- “Yes” for Neutered, “No” for Unneutered, “Unknown” if you can’t tell ![][image18] **Spot Last Seen** \-  Floor no. or other details of where the cat was seen **Date Last Seen** \- defaults to current date; is overrideable  **Caretaker** \- The person who feeds/looks after it, if known. **Notes** \- Other info about the cat (ex: tail length / eye color / collar / pregnant / behavior / sickness or injury description)  |  |

## **1.5 Editing or removing a cat in the session**

* **To edit:** tap the cat's card. The same form opens with its details — change what you need and press **Save**.  
* **To remove:** tap the **trash icon** on the card. This takes the cat out of this session.

![][image19]

**Figure 4:** *Edit Entry Form*

## **1.6 Finishing the session**

When you've logged every cat:

1\.   Tap **Finish** (mobile) or **Submit** (desktop).  
2\.   Confirm.

The session is now **Submitted** and goes to a manager to review. You generally don't need to touch it after this — if something needs fixing, a manager handles it during review.

![][image20]

**Figure 5:** *Finish Session Confirmation*

**To discard a session instead** (e.g. you started it by mistake): tap the **trash icon** near the Census No. and confirm. This deletes the unfinished session.

## **1.7 Quick reference**

* Count cats → **Sessions → Create New → pick location**.  
* Add a cat → **\+ / Add entry → fill the form → Save**.  
* Photo trouble → the cat is still saved; **Retry** or **Skip**.  
* Done → **Finish / Submit** (it goes to a manager).  
* Started by mistake → **trash icon → discard**.  
*  You can always press **Continue** an unfinished session later.  
* Something's broken → **your name → Report bug** (see 1.8).

## **1.8 Reporting a problem**

If something in the app looks wrong or doesn't work, you can tell the administrators without leaving the app — and without needing anyone's email address.

1\. Tap **your name** (top corner) to open your account details.  
2\. Under **"Noticed an issue?"**, tap **Report bug**.  
3\. Describe what happened — what you were doing, and what you expected instead. 
4\. Tap **Send report**.

That's it. The report goes straight to the administrators, who can see it in their Admin tab and mark it resolved once it's fixed. Your name goes with the report, so they can come back to you if they need more detail.

**Anyone can do this** — volunteers, managers, and administrators alike. If in doubt, report it; a duplicate report costs nothing.

# **PART 2 \- MANAGER** {#part-2---manager}

As a manager you can do everything a volunteer can, **plus** you review and approve what volunteers submit, and you have full control of the cat database. You're the quality gate: volunteers gather the data, you make it official.

## **2.1 Everything a volunteer can do**

A quick recap, so this Part stands on its own:

* **Sign in** with Google (you must have been invited by an administrator).  
* **Run a census session:** **Sessions → Create New → pick a location**, then **\+ / Add entry** to log each cat (photo, name, color, age, sex, sociability, condition, neutered, spot last seen, caretaker, notes) → **Save**. Tap a card to edit, the trash icon to remove. **Finish / Submit** when done; **Continue** an unfinished one later.  
* **View** the overview dashboard, the TNVR statistics, the cat database, and the public catalog.  
* **Report a problem** from your account details (section 1.8).

Everything in Part 1, sections 1.3–1.8, applies to you too. The rest of this Part is what's *new* for managers.

## **2.2 Reviewing submitted sessions**

When volunteers submit sessions, the cats they logged wait for your review.

1\.   Go to **Sessions** and tap **Review Sessions**.  
2\.   You'll see the **For Review** list — every cat awaiting review, with a count of how many are pending.

![][image21]

**Figure 6:** *Sessions Manager View*

For each cat you have two choices:

* **Quick approve** — tap the **✓ (check)** button. Confirm, and the cat is accepted as-is and added to the official database. Use this when the entry is clearly correct and not a duplicate.  
* **Full review** — tap the **✎ (pencil) / Review** button to open the two-step review:  
    
    
    
    
  


**Step 1 — Info Validation.** Correct any details the volunteer got wrong (color, age, sex, sociability, status, caretaker, notes, location). The **Region (override)** field lets you firmly assign the cat to a location. 

\- **Approve Instantly** ("New cat, Approve") — accept it as a brand-new cat. 

\- **Discard** — delete the entry entirely (use for junk/mistaken entries). 

\- **Next ›** — save your corrections and move to Step 2\.

![][image22]

**Figure 7:** *Info Validation Screen*

**Step 2 — Cross-Reference (check for duplicates).** The app shows existing cats (by default, those in the same location) so you can tell whether this is a cat you already have on record. \- If it **matches an existing cat**, tap **Merge ›** on that cat. A dialog shows the fields that differ — pick the correct value for each (matching fields merge automatically). Confirm, and the new sighting is folded into the existing record. \- If it's **genuinely new**, tap **New cat, Approve**. \- **Discard** removes it.

![][image23]

**Figure 8:** *Cross-Reference Screen*

Once approved or merged, the cat leaves the review queue.

## **2.3 The cat database — full control**

Open the **Database** tab. Unlike volunteers (who can only look), you can add, edit, and delete cats.

* **Add a cat directly:** tap **Add entry** (the **\+**). This opens the same entry form, outside of any session — useful for adding a cat you already know about.  
* **Delete a cat:** tap the **trash icon** on its card and confirm. This permanently removes it.  
* **Open a cat** to see three tabs:  
* **General** — identity and details: color, age, sex, sociability, status, **Region (override)**, caretaker, spot last seen, notes. You can also **change the photo** (including **rotating** it — see 1.4) and flip the **Adoptable** switch, which puts the cat on the **public Catalog**. That page is visible to anyone and findable through Google, so read section 2.6 before turning it on for a cat. Edit, then **Save changes** (or **Cancel**).  
*  **Medical** — **condition**, **neutered** (Yes/No/Unknown), **neuter date**, and **vaccination date**. Edit and **Save changes**.  
* **Interventions** — the cat's TNVR and veterinarian actions. Tap **New Intervention** to add one, and set each one's status (**Pending → Finished**, or **Cancelled**).

![][image24]

**Figure 9:** *Editable Cat Entry on Database*

The **Sheets** button on the Database screen opens the related Google Sheet in a new tab for reference.

## **2.4 Census Report**

The **Census Report** button (on the Sessions screen) opens the census report document in a new browser tab — the shared write-up used for reporting outside the app.

## **2.5 Editing the spreadsheet directly (emergency fallback)**

You — unlike volunteers — keep **edit access** to the Google Sheets. Because the sync is **two-way**, anything you change in the sheet flows back into the app on the next sync (every few minutes), and if the same cat changed in both places, the **most recent edit wins**.

**Use this sparingly.** The app is the safe, intended place to make changes — it validates your input and avoids conflicts. Edit the sheet directly only when the app isn't usable and something genuinely can't wait. A few cautions:

* Never change the format of the GSheets.  
* Don't touch the hidden/locked columns (they're protected for a reason).  
* Don’t clear/delete rows/sheets (do cat deletions on app).  
* A value the app wouldn't accept (a misspelled status, an invalid date) may be **rejected** when it syncs back — so stick to the same options the app offers.  
* When the app is available again, go back to working in it.  
* To replace a photo in the GSheets, make sure to insert the new image into the desired cell and that the cell does not have any formulas written like this: “IMAGE=url(...)”. That formula should be automatically overwritten on proper insert anyways.

### **Why a sheet's numbers sometimes skip (e.g. 1, 2, 3, 5)**

**Nothing is missing, and nothing needs fixing.** A gap in the first column is normal and permanent.

A cat's **Catalog No.** belongs to it for good. When a cat leaves a sheet — it's deleted, it's merged into another record as a duplicate, or it was being counted in the wrong region and the app moved it — the row goes, and **its number retires with it.** The next cat added to that sheet carries on from the highest number used, so the gap stays open.

That is deliberate. If the app reused an old number, every past mention of it — a vet record, a photo caption, a note in someone's phone — would suddenly point at a *different cat*. And if the app closed the gap by shifting everyone up, every cat below it would change number at once. Leaving the gap is the only option that keeps each cat's number meaning one cat, forever.

**One thing to watch:** because of this, **the highest number on a sheet is not the number of cats on it.** A sheet whose last row reads 15 may well hold 14 cats. To count cats, use the app — never the spreadsheet's numbering.

*A cat moved to another region keeps nothing of its old number: it joins the new sheet at the end, with that sheet's next number. This is correct — each region numbers its own cats from 1, so the old number would collide.*


 

 

## **2.6 The public Catalog — what the outside world sees**

The **Catalog** is a public web page. Anyone can open it without signing in, and **search engines like Google can now find it** — so treat what's on it as public writing about AGILA's cats.

**Which cats appear:** a cat shows up when its **Adoptable** switch is on (Database → the cat → General) *and* it has no status like Adopted, MIA, Fostered, or Deceased. Turning the switch off removes it from the Catalog within a few minutes.

**Each cat has its own page.** Tapping a cat in the Catalog opens a page just for that cat, with its own web address you can **copy and share** — in a group chat, a post, or a message to someone interested in adopting.

### **What the health information says — and why it sometimes says "Unknown"**

The Catalog shows four things about each cat's health, and it now reports them **honestly rather than optimistically**:

| Row | What you'll see |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Neutered** | Yes or No, taken straight from the **Neutered** field on the Medical tab |
| **Vaccinated** | **Yes**, **Expired**, or **Unknown** |
| **Sick** | Yes, No, or **Unknown** |
| **Injured** | Yes, No, or **Unknown** |

**"Unknown" means nobody has recorded it** — not that the answer is no. Previously the Catalog filled these gaps in with reassuring answers, which meant it could tell a member of the public that a cat was healthy and unvaccinated when the truth was simply that no one had checked. It no longer does that.

**"Expired" for vaccination** means the cat *was* vaccinated, but more than **a year** ago, so it is due again. It is not an alarm and it doesn't stop a cat being adopted — it's a reminder that a booster is owed.

**What to do about it:** if a cat reads **Unknown**, the fix is to record the real answer in **Database → the cat → Medical**. The Catalog updates on its own from there. Expect a good number of Unknowns at first — that's the true state of the records catching up, not a fault in the app.

**\[SCREENSHOT NEEDED: a public Catalog cat page showing the four health rows\]**

# **PART 3 \- ADMIN** {#part-3---admin}

As an administrator you can do everything a manager can, **plus** you manage the people, the locations, and the Google Sheets connection. You're the only role that sees the **Admin** tab.

## **3.1 Everything a manager (and volunteer) can do**

A quick recap, so this Part stands on its own:

* **Run and review census sessions** — create sessions and log cats (Part 1), and review, approve, merge, or discard what volunteers submit (Part 2, section 2.2).  
* **Manage the cat database** — add, edit, and delete cats across the General, Medical, and Interventions tabs; toggle Adoptable; change photos (Part 2, section 2.3).  
* **View** the Overview dashboard and TNVR statistics, open the **Census Report**, and (in a pinch) make emergency edits to the spreadsheet (Part 2, section 2.5).  
* **Report a problem** from your account details, like anyone else (Part 1, section 1.8) — though as an administrator you're also the one who reads those reports (section 3.5).

The rest of this Part is what's *new* for administrators: the **Admin** tab. It has six sections, in this order — **Users & Access**, **GSheet Config**, **Photo Storage**, **Bug Reports**, **Links**, and **Regions**.

![][image25]

**Figure 10:** *Admin Tab*

## **3.2 Users & Access — managing people**

This is how someone gets into the app at all: **you invite them here first.**

**To add a person:**

1\. Tap **Add Entry**. 

2\. Enter their **email** (the Google account they'll sign in with), an optional **name**, and their **role** (Volunteer, Manager, or Administrator). 

3\. Save. They can now **Sign in with Google** using that email.

**To change someone's role:** use the **role dropdown** on their row and pick the new role. The change takes effect immediately.

**To remove someone:** tap the **trash icon** on their row. They'll no longer be able to use the app.

![][image26]

**Figure 11:** *Admin Tab Users & Access Section*

**The three roles, in short:**

| Role | Can do |
| :---- | :---- |
| **Volunteer** | Run census sessions; view-only everywhere else. |
| **Manager** | All of the above \+ review/approve, full database control, census report. |
| **Administrator** | All of the above \+ this Admin tab. |

## **3.3 GSheet Config — the sync, and how to recover it**

This section controls the connection between the app and the Google Sheets. Most of the time you'll never touch it — but if the sync ever stops, this is where you fix it.

![][image28]

**Figure 12:** *Admin Tab GSheet Config Section*

### **Sync status — and "the sync is Frozen"**

The top of this section shows whether the sync is **Active** (green) or **Frozen** (red, with a reason).

**What "Frozen" means:** if a sync ever fails, the app **automatically freezes** the sync to avoid making things worse, and sends an alert (to a Discord channel). While frozen, the app and the sheets stop updating each other.

**How to recover — the most important procedure in this manual:**

1\. **Read the reason** shown next to the Frozen badge (and the Discord alert). It usually points at the cause — often a bad value someone typed into a sheet. 

2\. **Fix the cause** — correct the offending cell in the sheet, or the data in the app. 

3\. Tap **Unfreeze**. This runs a full re-sync from the sheets and then resumes normal syncing. 

4\. The status should return to **Active**.

If you're not sure what the reason means or the freeze comes straight back, this is the one situation to **ask a developer**.

### **Provision region sheets**

**Provision Sheets** re-applies the correct structure to every region's sheet (headers, protected columns, and the list of regions). It's **safe to run any time** — use it if a sheet's layout looks wrong or after fixing something manually. It does **not** change any cat data.

### **Seed missing UUIDs**

The **Seed UUIDs** button gives a permanent hidden ID to old sheet rows that don't have one yet, so they can be imported. This is essentially a **one-time, first-setup** action — after go-live, new rows get their ID automatically, and you should never need this again. Because it's identity-related, it asks you to confirm before running.

Provision and Seed are deliberately separate buttons: Provision is safe structural repair; Seed touches cat identity and is a once-at-setup step. When in doubt, only use**Provision**.

### **Retire sync — the permanent stop**

**This is not the same as Freeze, and it cannot be undone from the app.**

Freezing is a **pause**: something went wrong, you fix it, you press Unfreeze, and syncing resumes. **Retiring** is the deliberate end of the connection — for when AGILA decides to stop using the app and go back to working in the spreadsheets alone.

When you retire the sync:

* The app **stops writing to the spreadsheets entirely**, permanently.  
* The **column protections are released**, so the columns the app used to manage (the ID and timestamp columns) become editable by people again. This matters — without it you'd be left with a spreadsheet full of locked columns and no app to unlock them.  
* The cats stay in the app, and the spreadsheets keep everything they already had. **Nothing is deleted.**

Because it's permanent, the app asks you to type **RETIRE** to confirm.

**Only do this as a deliberate decision by AGILA, never as a way to stop a problem.** If sync is misbehaving, you want **Freeze**, not Retire. If you're unsure which you need, you need Freeze — and a developer.

**\[SCREENSHOT NEEDED: the Retire sync control and its typed confirmation\]**

## **3.4 Photo Storage — space, and how to free it**

Photos are the only thing in the app that grows meaningfully over time. This section shows how much space they're using **and** gives you the one button that frees some up.

### **The gauge**

A bar with the amount used and a percentage.

* **Green** — plenty of room, nothing to do.  
* **Amber** — getting full. Reclaim orphaned photos (below) and keep an eye on it.  
* **Red** — close to the limit. **Photo uploads will start failing** if it fills up. Reclaim first; if that doesn't free enough, ask a developer.

Underneath, **Last cleanup** tells you when the reclaim below was last run.

### **Reclaim orphaned photos**

Over time, deleting cats and merging duplicates can leave behind photo files that no cat record uses anymore. **Reclaim photos…** finds and deletes those leftovers, freeing up space.

It is **safe** — it only removes a photo that **no** cat points to, so a photo still shown anywhere in the app is never touched. It doesn't change any cat data. Because it deletes files, it asks you to confirm first, then reports how many it cleaned up.

Run it occasionally for housekeeping — say, after a big round of deletions or merges — or whenever the gauge turns amber. There's no harm in running it when there's nothing to clean; it'll just report "no orphans found".

**\[SCREENSHOT NEEDED: the Photo Storage card, showing the gauge and the Reclaim photos button\]**

## **3.5 Bug Reports — what people have told you**

When anyone reports a problem (Part 1, section 1.8), it lands here. The **Bug Reports** card on the Admin tab shows how many are still open; tapping through opens the full list.

For each report you can see who sent it and what they described, and you can:

* **Resolve** it once it's dealt with — it moves out of the open list.  
* **Reopen** it if the problem comes back.

Reports from someone who has since been removed from the app show as **Unknown reporter**; the report itself is kept.

There's no automatic notification, so **check this occasionally** — it's the only route your volunteers have to tell you something is broken.

## **3.6 Links — the buttons that point outside the app**

Some buttons in the app open documents that live outside it — the **Adopt / Foster Form** and the **Referral Sheet**. These used to be fixed and could only be changed by a developer. Now you can update them yourself.

1\. Open **Admin → Links**.  
2\. Paste the new web address into the field for the link you're changing.  
3\. Tap **Save links**.

The change takes effect immediately for everyone. If a form ever moves or a link breaks, this is the fix — no developer needed.

**\[SCREENSHOT NEEDED: the Links section\]**

## **3.7 Regions — managing locations**

A **region** is a named campus location (e.g. *GATE 3*, *ARETE*). Every cat and session belongs to one. Adding a region here also sets up its Google Sheet automatically — no developer needed.

* **Add a region:** tap **Add Region**, type the **name**, pick a **color**, and confirm.  
* **Rename a region:** tap the **pencil**, edit the name, and **Save**. (Its sheet is renamed to match, so syncing keeps working.)  
* **Delete a region:** tap the **trash icon**. You will **always** be asked to **type the region's name to confirm**, whether or not it still has cats in it. Deleting a region also removes the cats that belong *only* to that region, and removes its sheet tab.

![][image27]

**Figure 13:** *Admin Tab Regions Section*

**\!\!\!** **Never create a region by adding a tab directly in the Google Sheet.** Always add regions here in the app — that's the only way the sheet gets set up correctly.
